subject: research/swe-orgs
professional: a senior empirical software-engineering researcher (ICSE/FSE programme-committee level, qualitative coding and mining-software-repositories methods); first checks: were the sources actually read, is the coding of evidence and transfer done with more than one coder and an agreement statistic, is the keyword classifier validated against hand labels (precision and recall), do the published numbers reproduce from the committed script and data, and is the nearest prior work on LLM multi-agent organisations and their failure taxonomies cited

evidence.correctness: The arithmetic is right: an independent recount (scratchpad swe-orgs/indep.py, no import of swe_orgs, own regex loop and Newcombe closed-form Wilson) on the full ledger gives exactly the counts run.py prints today (coordination 147, unlanded 50, unverified 31, tooling 203, rework 141, duplicate 95 of 9,037 rows), and a hand Wilson for 25/1942 gives 0.87% to 1.89%, matching results.txt's 0.9% to 1.9%. The evidence and transfer tallies in the README match the CSVs (5 measured, 2 survey, 8 case, 2 postmortem, 2 regulatory, 29 practitioner, 13 opinion; 21/38/2). But the committed results.txt (1,942 rows) cannot be reproduced exactly: no ledger cutoff is recorded, and files dated up to 2026-10-21 give 2,067 rows with tooling 26 and rework 19 against 25 and 18. More seriously, what the numbers claim to measure is not measured: a hand label of 8 random coordination matches found 4 are not inter-session coordination (a 'parallel-pull' shell command, a 'synthetic trace' matched by 'race', an in-run multiprocessing race, a test suite run in parallel), and 65% (180/276) of error-reporting rows at the snapshot and 75% (1,665/2,232) today match no class at all. Capped at 2: reproducible computation, invalid measurement.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: the 61-practice and 60-source CSVs with every documented column (validate() returns no problems), run.py scoring against prompts/runs/ (runs in 0.6 s on 9,037 rows), the open-candidate rule, the Wilson intervals, the figure (failure_classes.svg exists and is parsed from results.txt by figure.py), the LOG with 22 batch entries, and the tests. All work end to end. The README honestly calls this 'preliminary' and 'not the finished catalogue'. Gaps: results.txt and the figure were last regenerated at 1,942 rows (ledger now 9,037), and the README's own next steps (hand-label ledger errors, read papers in full) have not started since batch 22 (2026-10-21, the last commit under the subject).
evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests` -> 9 passed in 0.21 s. The file defines 10 test functions: test_readme_counts_match_the_csvs is defined twice (tests/test_catalogue.py:54 and :87), so the first (which checks the transfer counts and 'The catalogue has N rows') is shadowed and never runs; run standalone it passes. Five seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 survived (dropping the Wilson z^2/4n^2 term, partial transfer weight 0.5 -> 1.0, removing 'missing|bug' from the tooling class, the open-candidate threshold 0.05 -> 0.5 in run.py), 1 caught (reversing the priority sort). run.py is not exercised by any test, and most of the suite checks that README prose matches CSV counts rather than the scoring logic.
evidence.craft: Read src/swe_orgs/catalogue.py (96 lines), experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, tests/test_catalogue.py. The code is short and readable and stdlib-only. Defects: duplicate test function name silently drops a test; the regexes are unanchored substrings, so 'race' matches 'trace'/'embrace' (15 error strings in the ledger contain such a substring) and 'bug' matches 'debug'; error_texts iterates characters if `errors` is ever a string (none in today's ledger, so latent); the 5% candidate threshold is a magic number inside a print loop in run.py:27 rather than a named, tested function; results.txt records no ledger cutoff or commit, so it cannot be regenerated.
evidence.claims: README.md:3 says 'All numbers below come from experiments/results.txt', but README.md:23 reports 'Of 1900 runs, 254 reported any error', unlanded 1.3%, unverified 0.4%, duplicate 0.6 to 1.6%, while results.txt says 1,942 rows, 258, 1.2%, 0.5%, 0.7 to 1.6%. README.md:24 says P23 has 'a 4.0% priority' (results.txt: 1.3%) and 'tooling is the largest class (2.5% of 751 runs)'. The homepage summary (research/_homepage/projects.json:3382) says 'four measured' (CSV: 5), 'the 1,261-row run ledger' and 'Eighteenth batch' (LOG: batch 22). Backed claims: the evidence-type and transfer tallies, the GitLab/Knight Capital failure descriptions (consistent with the SEC order and GitLab postmortem as publicly known), Sadowski et al. ICSE-SEIP 2018 pp. 181-190 doi 10.1145/3183519.3183525 and Wilson (1927) JASA 22(158):209-212 are correct citations. Limits are disclosed honestly (web-search-only verification, keyword classes unvalidated, 5% cutoff arbitrary). The headline negative result still holds on today's ledger (largest class 2.2% < 5%), but several printed figures a reader would quote are wrong.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could use data/practices.csv as an annotated reading list with transfer judgments, which is the useful artefact. They could not build on the quantitative part: the ceiling is the same for every practice in a class, so 'priority' is just class share times a three-level weight; the classifier covers a quarter of reported errors with about half precision on a sample; failure cost is ignored. Nearest prior work: Forsgren, Humble and Kim (Accelerate/DORA, cited), and on the agent side MetaGPT (Hong et al., ICLR 2024, encoding company SOPs and roles into LLM agents), ChatDev (Qian et al., ACL 2024, a waterfall software company of agents) and Cemri et al. 2025, 'Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?' (MAST, a failure taxonomy built from hand-annotated traces with inter-annotator agreement), none of which is cited (grep of sources.csv, README and LOG). The question (which human-org practices transfer to an agent fleet) is reasonable but the result is neither new relative to MetaGPT/ChatDev/MAST nor soundly measured; far from the PhD/publishable bar in research/CLAUDE.md and PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.domain: Against standard empirical-SE practice for qualitative catalogues and log mining: evidence and transfer labels are one coder's reading of search summaries with no agreement statistic (Cohen's kappa) and no second rater; 51 of 60 sources are only 'partly' checked, one 'no', and no paper was read in full; the keyword classifier was never validated (no precision/recall on a hand-labelled sample, which the README itself lists as a next step); a 5% threshold is applied to a measure whose recall is unknown and at most 25% coverage of error rows, so the negative result 'no practice clears the bar' is an artefact as much as a finding; self-reported errors miss silent failures (disclosed); there is no multiple-comparison issue since nothing is tested, but no uncertainty from classification error is propagated either. A senior reviewer would reject the quantitative claim and accept the catalogue only as a preliminary literature map.

defects.what: The headline negative result ('no failure class reaches 5%, so no proposal') rests on an unvalidated keyword classifier that matches no class for 65% of error-reporting rows at the snapshot and 75% today, with about 50% precision on a hand-labelled sample of the coordination class; the bar is applied to a measure of unknown recall
README says all numbers come from results.txt, but its results paragraph reports 1900 runs / 254 errors and class shares and intervals that differ from results.txt (1942 / 258)
README quotes P23 at 'a 4.0% priority' and tooling at '2.5% of 751 runs'; results.txt gives 1.3% on 1,942 rows
Homepage summary says 'four measured', 'the 1,261-row run ledger' and 'Eighteenth batch'; the CSV has 5 measured, results.txt 1,942 rows, the LOG 22 batches
test_readme_counts_match_the_csvs is defined twice; the first definition (transfer counts and 'The catalogue has N rows') is shadowed and never runs
Scoring and run.py are nearly untested: 4 of 5 seeded mutations survive (Wilson term, partial weight, tooling keywords, 5% candidate threshold); run.py has no test
Nearest prior work on LLM agent organisations and their failure taxonomies (MetaGPT, ChatDev, Cemri et al. 2025 MAST) is not cited, so novelty and the classification method are not positioned
Evidence and transfer labels are single-coder judgments from search summaries; no paper read in full, 52 of 60 sources only partly or not checked, no inter-rater agreement

verdict: A small, honest, stdlib-only literature catalogue (61 practices from 60 sources, each tagged with evidence type, transfer and the assumption that fails for agents) with a scorer whose arithmetic reproduces exactly on an independent recount of the 9,037-row ledger. It misses the bar on claims, verification, fitness and domain. The README and homepage quote figures that match neither results.txt nor the CSV (1900 vs 1942 runs, P23 at 4.0% vs 1.3%, 'four measured' vs 5, a 1,261-row ledger), one test is silently shadowed and 4 of 5 seeded bugs survive. The quantitative headline, that no failure class reaches 5% so nothing should change, rests on a keyword classifier that leaves 65 to 75% of reported errors unclassified and was about 50% precise on a hand sample. The sources were checked by web search only, coded by one reader, and the agent-organisation literature (MetaGPT, ChatDev, MAST) is not cited. Useful as a reading list; not a research result a senior empirical-SE reviewer would sign off on.
